newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firmer as yen slides.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firmer as yen slides.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished firm but off their highs on Thursday as participants fixed their gaze on the yen's sharp decline against the dollar following comments by a key Japanese Ministry of Finance (MOF) official.
Nikkei 225 September futures ended 220 points higher at 20,585, almost 200 points below their peak of 20,780, on active volume of 23,000 lots. June ended at 20,540 on 9,000 lots.
"Trading the Nikkei today was like trading the dollar/yen. After Sakakibara's comments, there was just a lot of short-covering in dollar/yen," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
The dollar shot up, after falling to a seven-month low of 110.62 yen overnight, on a comment by the MOF's Eisuke Sakakibara who said Japan was not ready to raise interest rates.

The rally was fuelled by a former MOF official saying Sakakibara favoured a yen rate slightly stronger than 120 yen to the dollar. The U.S. unit was quoted at 114.01/11 yen at 0715 GMT after hitting a high of 115.80 yen.
The trader said Thursday's gains on the Nikkei share average were led by banking shares, which had been oversold recently.
"There are still quite a lot of worries in the minds of Nikkei traders because there's a risk the dollar/yen could come off as quickly as it rose," he said.
He said the September Nikkei should trade in a broader 20,200-20,800 range unless the dollar moved sharply against the yen in New York trade.
"I think most contracts have already been rolled over to September. So tomorrow's SQ (special quotation for settlement of June futures) shouldn't have a big impact," he added.
On Taiwan futures, the June MSCI contract ended at 353.6 against its opening 351.8 on volume of 1,304 lots.
